chunks: Ahmad, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The pilgrim does not cease to have upon him the light of the Hajj as long as he does not commit a sin.

key_terms.نُورُ الْحَجِّ: The light of Hajj, referring to the spiritual illumination or merit acquired through pilgrimage
key_terms.يُلِمَّ بِذَنْبٍ: To commit or touch upon a sin, implying the act of sinning

ai.seo_question: What happens to the spiritual light of Hajj if a pilgrim sins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the spiritual radiance (nur) bestowed by Hajj persists as long as the pilgrim remains free from major sins, a concept central to Shia asceticism regarding the fragility of spiritual states. This narration underscores the dynamic nature of divine grace, linking the ritual act of pilgrimage directly to moral vigilance and the preservation of inner purity.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Abu Muhammad Al Hajjal, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The pilgrim is such that the Light of the Hajj does not cease to be upon him for as long as he does not sin’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad has narrated from abu Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn abu Yazid from those whom he has mentioned who has said the foiiowing: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
a pilgrim continues to live with the light of al-Hajj until he commits sins again and again.’”
